questions.question: The Khalji Dynasty ruled over Delhi from ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1290 to 1320.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Khalji Dynasty- was the second ruling family of the Delhi sultanate, a Muslim kingdom in north India.
 
• **The Khalji dynasty ruled from 1290 to 1320.**
 
• It was founded by Jalal ud din Firuz Khalji and came to power in a revolution that signified the transfer of authority from Turkic nobility to Afghans.
 
• Alauddin Khalji made serious efforts to re-assess the land revenue and unify the taxes not only in rural areas but also in urban areas.
 
• He established a centralised administrative system of revenue collection. 
 
• Muqtis were appointed for revenue collection.
 
• Alauddin made sure that their offices were not hereditary.
 
• He kept proper control over them.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Khalji Dynasty:

 
 
• Founder: Jalal-ud-din Firoz Khilji
 
• The Khilji dynasty started from 1290 to 1320 AD.
 
• Famous ruler: Ala-ud-din Khilji
 
• Last ruler: Quṭb al-Din Mubarak Shah

questions.question: Who among the following was the Sultan of Delhi when Bahmani kingdom was founded in 1347 CE?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Muhammad bin Tughlaq**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Muhammad bin Tughlaq** was the Sultan of Delhi from **1325 CE to 1351 CE**.
 
• He was a ruler of the **Tughlaq dynasty** and succeeded his father, **Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq**.
 
• During his reign, the **Bahmani Kingdom** was established in 1347 CE in the **Deccan region** by **Alauddin Bahman Shah**, marking the beginning of an independent Muslim state in South India.
 
• Muhammad bin Tughlaq is known for his ambitious and often controversial policies, including the shifting of his capital from **Delhi to Daulatabad** and introducing token currency.
 
• His reign was marked by administrative reforms, but many of them failed due to **poor implementation**.
 
• He faced several revolts during his rule, including the revolt that led to the establishment of the **Bahmani Kingdom**.
 
• Despite his failures, Muhammad bin Tughlaq is remembered as a ruler with **visionary ideas**, albeit ahead of his time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mubarak Shah Khalji**__

 __
 
• **Mubarak Shah Khalji** was a ruler of the **Khalji dynasty** and reigned from **1316 to 1320 CE**.
 
• He was the last ruler of the Khalji dynasty before the establishment of the **Tughlaq dynasty.**
 
• His reign was marked by internal strife and instability, which ultimately led to his assassination.
 
 
 
• **Bahlul Lodi**__
 __
 
• **Bahlul Lodi** was the founder of the **Lodi dynasty**, which succeeded the Tughlaq dynasty in **1451 CE**.
 
• He ruled Delhi as Sultan and worked to consolidate his authority over North India.
 
• The Lodi dynasty marked the last phase of the Delhi Sultanate before the advent of the **Mughal Empire.**
 
 
 
• **Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq**__
 
 
• **Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq** was the founder of the **Tughlaq dynasty** and ruled from **1320 CE to 1325 CE.**
 
• He is remembered for his administrative reforms and attempts to stabilize the Sultanate after the turbulent reign of the Khalji dynasty.
 
• His reign saw the construction of the **Tughlaqabad Fort** in Delhi.

questions.question: Raziya Sultan was the daughter of _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Iltutmish**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Raziya Sultan was the first female Muslim ruler of South Asia and ruled from 1236 to 1240.
 
• Raziya was the only daughter among the four children** of Iltutmish**, the third ruler of the Delhi Sultanate.
 
• Her mother was Turkan Khatoon, the daughter of Qutbuddin Aibak (r.1206-10) – the first ruler of the Delhi Sultanate.
 
• Iltutmish nominated Razia as his successor after the death of his most capable son, Prince Nasiruddin Mahmud.
 
• Various sources confirm that Iltutmish selected Raziya as she was the eldest of his surviving children and had already displayed her deserving political insights.
 
• She was from Turkish Seljuk’s ancestry and came to be the fifth Mumluk Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate.
 
• Raziya’s accession to the throne was solely based on her merit and was a significant departure in the then political climate where the throne was considered a male monopoly.
 
• The Muslim theologians approved her ascension and most of the Turkish nobility, army, and people of Delhi accepted her on the throne is a testimony of the politico-cultural spirit of that age.
 
• Raziya remains one of the most significant icons of women's power in the history of India.
 
• Her chief merit lies in her fearless assertive decisions, her ability to rule by integrating all walks of people, and to rise above the prejudices of her age and times.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**The Delhi Sultanate **

 
• It refers to the five Muslim kingdoms of Turkic and Pashtun (Afghan) origin that ruled the territory of Delhi between 1206 and 1526 CE. In the 16th century, the last of their line was overthrown by the Mughals, who established the Mughal Empire in India.
 
• The five dynasties included:
 
 
• the Mamluk Dynasty (1206–1290)
 
• the Khilji Dynasty (1290–1320)
 
• the Tughlaq Dynasty (1320–1414)
 
• the Sayyid Dynasty (1414–1451)
 
• the Afghan Lodi Dynasty (1451–1526)

questions.question: Which of the following dynasties ruled over Delhi just after the Sayyid dynasty?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lodi dynasty**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Lodi dynasty **was **an Afghan dynasty **that **ruled the Delhi Sultanate **from **1451 to 1526**.
 
• It was **the fifth and final dynasty **of the **Delhi Sultanate **and was **founded by Bahlul Khan Lodi **when he **replaced the Sayyid dynasty**.
 
• The **dynasty **was of **Afghan origin**. The **first Lodī ruler **was **Bahlul Lodi(reigned 1451–89), **the **most powerful **of the **Punjab chiefs**, who **replaced **the **last king **of the **Sayyid dynasty in 1451**.
 
• **The Mughal emperor Babur defeated **and **killed Ibrahim Lodi **in the **Battle of Panipat**. The **death of Ibrahim Lodi **brought the **320-year-long Delhi Sultanate **to an **end**, and the **Mughal Empire took its place**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Khalji **or **Khilji dynasty **was a **Turco-Afghan dynasty **that **ruled the Delhi sultanate**, covering **large parts **of the **Indian subcontinent **for nearly **three decades between 1290 and 1320**.
 
• The **four major Rajput dynasties**—**Pratihara, Paramara, Chauhan, and Caulukya**—**claimed Agnikula lineage**.
 
• The **Tughlaq dynasty**, also referred to as **Tughluq or Tughluk dynasty**, was **a Muslim dynasty **of **Turkic origin **that ruled over **the Delhi sultanate **in **medieval India**. Its **reign started in 1320 in Delhi **when **Ghazi Malik assumed **the **throne **under the title of **Ghiyath al-Din Tughluq. **The **dynasty ended in 1413**.

questions.question: Which monument of Khilji dynasty in Delhi has the utilization of red sandstone?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Alai Darwaza**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Alai Darwaza **is a monument built during **the Khilji dynasty in Delhi **and it is made of red sandstone.
 
• The monument was built by Alauddin Khilji in 1311 AD and it served as the main entrance to the Qutub Complex.
 
• The architecture of the monument is a blend of Islamic and Hindu styles and it is decorated with intricate carvings and calligraphy.
 
• The Alai Darwaza is considered as one of the finest examples of Indo-Islamic architecture in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Victoria Memorial is a monument located in Kolkata, West Bengal, and it was built during the British Raj in memory of Queen Victoria.
 
• Charminar is a monument located in Hyderabad, Telangana, and it was built during the Qutb Shahi dynasty in 1591 AD. It is made of granite and limestone.
 
• Moti Masjid is a mosque located in the Red Fort complex in Delhi and it was built by Mughal emperor Aurangzeb in the 17th century. It is made of white marble.

questions.question: Who among the following introduced the silver tanka and the copper Jital - the two basic coins of the Sultanate period?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Iltumish.__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Iltutmish **introduced the** Silver Tanka and Copper Jital, the two coins of the Delhi Sultanate.**
 
• The coins prior to Iltutmish were** introduced by the Rulers which bear the Sanskrit characters and even Bull and Shivalinga.**
 
• Iltutmish was the first to introduce a **“Pure Arabic Coin” in India.**
 
• The Coins were engraved with** “The Mighty Sultan, Sun of the Empire and the Faith, Conquest-laden, Iltumish,”** after he received an investiture of **Sovereign Sultan of Delhi from the Caliph of Baghdad.**
 
• The Silver Tanka issued by **Iltutmish was weighing 175 grains.**
 
• **Gold Tanka **of the same** weight was later issued by Balban.**

questions.question: Who among the following was NOT a ruler of the Tughlaq dynasty?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rukunuddin Tughlaq**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Rukunuddin Tughlaq was a ruler of the Delhi sultanate for less than **seven months in 1236**.
 
• He belongs to the **slave dynasty**.
 
• He ascended the throne after the death of his father **Iltutmish**.
 
• The misadministration led to rebellions against Ruknuddin and was arrested and imprisoned.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** __**Muhammad-Bin-Tughlaq**__

__
 
• Jauna Khan succeeded his father in AD 1325 under the title of Muhammad- bin-Tughlaq.
 
• He was the most learned scholar of his time and knew both Arabic and Persian and had a comprehensive knowledge of philosophy, astronomy, logic, mathematics, and physical science.
 
• The Sultan maintained good relationships with foreigners and received an envoy from the Chinese ruler.
 
• Toghan Timur (AD 1341), came to seek permission to rebuild Buddhist Monasteries, in the Himalayan region which was destroyed during the crucial expedition.
 
• The Sultan gave permission and sent Ibn Battuta to the court of the Chinese emperor in 1347.
 
• Ibn Battuta was a traveler from Morocco. 

**Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq**__

__
 
• He was the founder of the Tughlaq dynasty.
 
• His father was a Turk and his mother was a Jat woman of Punjab.
 
• He founded the city of Tughlaqabad.
 
• He died in 1325, from the collapse of a wooden pavilion.
 
• The tomb of Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq (situated near Tuglaqabad fort) is the first tomb constructed within the walled enclosure which is polygonal in shape.

**​Firuz Shah Tughlaq**__

 
• Sultan Firoz Shah Tughlaq was a Muslim ruler of the Tughlaq dynasty and he reigned over the Sultanate of Delhi.
 
• He ruled from 1351 to 1388.
 
• Sultan Firoz Shah Tughlaq was forced by rebellions to concede virtual independence to Bengal and other provinces.
 
• Tughlaq established Sharia across his realm.
 
• Firoz Shah Tughlaq's autobiography is titled Futuhat-e-firozshahi.

questions.question: The famous Qila-i-Kuhna (mosque of the old fort) was built by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sher Shah**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Qila-i-Kuhna Mosque was built by **Sher Shah Suri**, the founder of the Suri Empire in India.
 
• It is located inside the Purana Qila (Old Fort) in Delhi, India.
 
• The mosque was constructed in **1541** during the short reign of Sher Shah Suri.
 
• It is an excellent example of early Mughal architecture, showcasing a blend of Indo-Islamic design elements.
 
• The mosque features a single domed prayer hall and is noted for its intricate stone carvings and decorative elements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sher Shah Suri:**

 
 
• Sher Shah Suri, originally named Farid Khan, was a prominent ruler of the Suri Dynasty in North India.
 
• He is best known for his administrative reforms and the introduction of the "Rupiya," which was the precursor to the modern rupee.
 
• Sher Shah's reign is marked by significant infrastructure projects, including the construction of the Grand Trunk Road.
 
 
 
• **Purana Qila:**
 
 
• Purana Qila, also known as the Old Fort, is one of the oldest forts in Delhi, built by Sher Shah Suri and his predecessor Humayun.
 
• The fort is believed to be located at the site of Indraprastha, the legendary city of the Pandavas from the Mahabharata.
 
• It features massive walls, several gateways, and other historical monuments within its premises.
 
 
 
• **Mughal Architecture:**
 
 
• Mughal architecture is a distinctive Indo-Islamic architectural style that developed in the Indian subcontinent during the Mughal Empire (1526–1857).
 
• It is characterized by large bulbous domes, slender minarets, massive halls, large vaulted gateways, and delicate ornamentation.
 
• Notable examples include the Taj Mahal, Red Fort, and Humayun's Tomb.
 
 
 
• **Indo-Islamic Architecture:**
 
 
• Indo-Islamic architecture is a blend of Indian and Islamic architectural styles.
 
• It features elements such as arches, domes, minarets, and intricate geometric and floral patterns.
 
• This style emerged during the Delhi Sultanate and reached its zenith during the Mughal period.
